title: Chicken drumstick, fried, coated, skin/coating not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: A chicken drumstick that is deep‑fried in a crispy coating. The skin and coating are usually removed before eating. This item is a staple in fast‑food and quick‑serve restaurant menus.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks are a popular fast‑food item because they are juicy and quick to prepare.
The coating often contains a blend of flour, spices, and breadcrumbs, giving it a golden crunch.
Deep‑frying is done at 175‑190 °C (350‑375 °F), creating a crisp crust while sealing in moisture.
In many regions the drumsticks are served with barbecue, honey‑mustard, or spicy chili sauces.
While chicken provides lean protein, frying adds extra fat content.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken drumsticks supply high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat provides niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Chicken contains phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bone health and immune function.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: Protein and a modest amount of fat help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Chicken meat is generally easy on the digestive system, fitting most dietary patterns.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds significant saturated and trans fats, which can raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Coatings often contain salt and flavor enhancers, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to chicken proteins.

items.title: Frying by‑products
items.content: Overheating oil can produce acrylamide and other potentially harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Remove the coating and skin before consumption, leaving the tender meat. The drumstick can be split, dipped in sauce, or added to salads and sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked drumsticks in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag at –18 °C (0 °F) where they remain good for about 2 months.
